info.title: OpenSim engine
info.description:
The grids, the simulators and the services of an install, and what is in the databases of a grid, as JSON:API resources; the errors are problem details (RFC 9457).

A list takes `search`, `sort` (`-` before a column for the descending order), `filter[<name>]`, `page[number]` and `page[size]`.

## Authentication

The API is closed: what manages the machine and the grids (the resources, the tasks, the health) needs an API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key is made on the machine and shown once: `opensim api-key create <label>`; `opensim api-key list` lists them without what opens them, `opensim api-key revoke <id>` closes one. A key opens everything for now. To try the API from this documentation, open the [test page](try.html), enter the address of the API and click Authorize.

What the viewers, the simulators and the visitors of a site call needs none (the message of the day, the guide, the pictures, the status of the grid, the pages): the operations marked as open. The calls in a format of OpenSimulator and the viewers (search, registration, offline messages, currency, land tools) are protected by what the protocol has: the secure session of an avatar, the secret of a region, the key of the money server.

servers.description: Where the application that uses the engine mounts the API

tags.name: Grids
tags.description: A grid run from this machine, only described here (a grid joined on another machine), or a standalone (one simulator that serves it all).

tags.name: Simulators
tags.description: A simulator is identified by its address (host:port); its slug has its grid (`vonda_welcome`).

tags.name: Services
tags.description:
What the simulators and the users of a grid ask for: the assets, the profiles, the login, the search. A service is served by a Robust of the grid, by the simulator of a standalone, or by a web site (the helpers) at an address the config of the grid gives.

`get-grid-info` is the /get_grid_info that Robust answers: the engine reads it, it does not provide one.

`kind` says who fixes the format of a web service: `fixed` (OpenSimulator or the viewers: only the address is the grid's to choose, and the format is described in this contract as an endpoint of its own) or `standard` (the engine's own; `standard` is its address, `legacy` the script that answered it before). `endpoint` is where the engine serves it.

tags.name: Archives
tags.description: The inventories (`iar`) and the regions (`oar`) the consoles of the simulators saved, in the data folder of their grid, and the backups of the setup (`backup`: the configuration, the data and the databases of a grid or of a simulator, `.tar.gz`). A file says what is in it by its name; they are read here, made by `opensim save iar|oar` and `opensim backup`.

tags.name: Avatars
tags.description: Read from the databases of the grid, each in the one of its service. An avatar is made with its account, its password, its inventory and its default outfit. Its name does not change.

tags.name: Regions
tags.description: The regions the grid knows (its table of regions) and the ones its simulators describe.

tags.name: Parcels
tags.description: The land of every simulator of the grid, read in the database of each.

tags.name: Estates
tags.description: The estates of the grid when its Robust serves them, else the ones of each simulator.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: What the grid keeps in its asset service: textures, sounds, notecards, scripts, objects... A record never carries its data: an image of any type (texture, TGA, JPEG) is asked as a picture (`/grids/{grid}/assets/{id}.{format}`, the grid keeps textures as JPEG 2000 and the engine converts them and keeps the result for a day), the other types as they are.

tags.name: Destinations
tags.description: The places the guide of the grid shows, by category, in the order of its source (`GuideSource` of `[Helpers]`: a file or a URL of "Name|Region URL" lines). The same list feeds the page of the guide and the boards of the scripts.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Cron and pseudo cron: each task has a name and an interval, runs when due, never twice at once, and a failure waits for its next turn. Asked to run, a task runs now. The search registers two: `search-parse` (once a minute: reads the snapshots of the registered simulators that are due) and `events-parse` (every 55 minutes: reads the calendar of events).

tags.name: Forms
tags.description: The fields of the forms (grid, remote-grid, simulator, region), in the standard format of the forms: name, label, type, default, options, condition, follows, group. Whoever shows a form (the terminal, a web page) reads them from here; the engine itself uses them to work out what is not answered.

tags.name: Fonts
tags.description: The names to give as `font` of a text image (`/text-images`).

tags.name: Search
tags.description: The search of the grid, made by the helpers: the simulators register to it and tell it their regions (a snapshot the helpers read), the viewers ask it for places, popular places, land for sale, events and classifieds. The format is the one of the module OpenSimSearch of the simulators; the address is the grid's to choose (`SearchURL` of `[Search]` and `DATA_SRV_*` of `[DataSnapshot]` in OpenSim.ini). A search can be shared by several grids: `gk`, the gatekeeper of the grid that asks, tells for which the search is made (the viewers do not send it). These calls need no API key: the viewers and the simulators do not send one.

tags.name: Economy
tags.description: The currency and the land tools of the grid, as the viewers and the money modules call them: XML-RPC at `currency.php` and `landtool.php` under the economy address the grid gives its viewers (`economy` of `[GridInfoService]`). Nothing is served without the key of the grid (`MoneyScriptAccessKey` of `[MoneyServer]`): a quote is tied to its purchase with it and to the address of who asked. An avatar proves who they are with their secure session, a region with its secret: no API key is needed, the viewers do not send one.

tags.name: Offline messages
tags.description: The messages for the avatars who are not there, with the module V1 of the simulators (`OfflineMessageModule = OfflineMessageModule`, `OfflineMessageURL` of `[Messaging]`), which posts them here in XML. The messages are kept in the table of the offline messages of Robust, the one its module V2 uses; an avatar who asked for it in their viewer also gets them by email. The other choice is the module V2 and the service of Robust, which needs none of this: with the helpers, the messages are mailed on request and none is lost; with Robust, nothing more is run, no mail is sent and 25 messages are kept per avatar.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Whether the grid and its web services answer as they should.

tags.name: Addresses
tags.description: Where the services of the grid are, and what the grid says of itself. The engine reads them from the files of the grid and from its `get_grid_info`, and gives them to the helpers, the manager and the plugins, which do not read the config again.

tags.name: Monitor
tags.description: The state of the grid at a glance: its Robust, its simulators (on this machine and elsewhere), its regions, who is in world. As data, as the lines of `opensim status`, or as a picture for a prim. The diagnosis, address by address, is the health.

tags.name: Message of the day
tags.description: The text the viewers show at login.

tags.name: Text images
tags.description: Pictures of a text, for the signs and the boards in world.

tags.name: Pages
tags.description: The pages the helpers show to the people, in HTML, at the addresses the grid gives (`GridInfoService` and `LoginService` in Robust.ini). They are made from the resources of this API: the guide shows `/grids/{grid}/destinations`, the profile an avatar.

tags.name: Grid info
tags.description: What Robust itself serves, which the engine reads.

tags.name: Setup
tags.description: The rules of the setup, for the tools that make a grid: from a few answers, the whole setup they stand for and what is wrong with them. Nothing is written, the tool shows the setup, asks again what is wrong and applies it.

get.description: The addresses the config of the grid gives (the services of Robust, the web services, the pages), what the grid says of itself at `get_grid_info`, and the ones that are expected and not given, asked now: a service that must refuse a call without data refuses it, and answers one that makes sense. The PHP extensions the engine needs and the files it reads come with them. `level` is `error` when something does not answer as it should, `ok` when all that is asked does, `none` when there is nothing to ask. The groups are the sections of the files of the grid; each row has the address, the status (the HTTP code, or the error), the time in milliseconds and its own level.

get.description: What the module of search of a simulator calls (`DATA_SRV_<grid>` of `[DataSnapshot]` is the address): a GET with the host and the port **of the simulator**, not those of the grid. The answer is nothing: the simulator waits for it to go on starting. The helpers read its snapshot once the answer is sent, after a pause for its regions to load, and again soon after; one that does not answer is read less and less often, then forgotten. `offline` forgets it and what it told.

parameters.description: The host of the simulator (not the grid's)

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The HTTP port of the simulator (not the grid's)

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: `online` when the simulator starts, `offline` when it stops

post.description:
The questions of the viewers and of the simulators to the search. XML-RPC, as the module OpenSimSearch speaks it: the body is a method call with one struct, the answer a struct with `success`, `errorMessage` and the rows in `data` (nothing in `data` when there is no result or it failed). The grid has the status of a failure only when the request is not understood or the search is not there.

### `dir_places_query`

The places (parcels shown in search) whose name or description has the words.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | The words, separated by spaces |
| `flags` | integer | The rating the viewer wants: bits 24 (PG), 25 (Mature), 26 (Adult); bit 10 asks the order by traffic |
| `category` | integer | The category of the places, 0 for any |
| `query_start` | integer | The row to start from, 101 are given at most |

**Answer** (each row of `data`)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parcel_id` | string | The identifier the viewer shows the place by |
| `name` | string | The name of the parcel |
| `for_sale` | string | Always False: the land for sale is another question |
| `auction` | string | Always False |
| `dwell` | number | Its traffic |
| `regionname` | string | The region it is in; the other columns of the parcel and of its region come with it |

### `dir_popular_query`

The popular places, by traffic.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | Words of the name, empty for all |
| `flags` | integer | Bit 12 asks the places that have a picture; bits 24 to 26 the rating |
| `query_start` | integer | The row to start from, 100 are given at most |
| `include_hypergrid` | string | `false` keeps the places of the other grids out |
| `include_landsales` | string | `true` adds the land for sale |
| `gatekeeper_url` | string | The grid the search is made for, when the address does not say it (`gk`) |

**Answer** (each row of `data`)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parcel_id` | string | The identifier of the place |
| `name` | string | The name |
| `dwell` | number | Its traffic |
| `gatekeeperURL` | string | The grid it belongs to |
| `regionname` | string | The region it is in |
| `regionUUID` | string | The UUID of the region |
| `landingpoint` | string | Where an avatar lands |
| `imageUUID` | string | Its picture |

### `dir_land_query`

The land for sale.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flags` | integer | Bits 24 to 26 the rating; 20 asks a price limit, 21 an area limit; the order is bit 15 (ascending), 16 (price), 18 (area), 19 (name), by price per meter by default |
| `type` | integer | The kind of land: 4294967295 for any, bits 3 and 4 for the mainland or an estate, auctions are not listed |
| `price` | integer | The highest price, when flags asks it |
| `area` | integer | The smallest area, when flags asks it |
| `query_start` | integer | The row to start from, 101 are given at most |

**Answer** (each row of `data`)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parcel_id` | string | The identifier of the parcel |
| `name` | string | Its name |
| `auction` | string | Always false |
| `for_sale` | string | Always true |
| `sale_price` | integer | Its price |
| `landing_point` | string | Where an avatar lands |
| `region_UUID` | string | The region it is in |
| `area` | integer | Its area in square meters |

### `dir_events_query`

The events of a day, or the ones to come.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | `day\|category\|words`: the day is a number of days from today, or `u` for the events to come and in progress; the category 0 for any |
| `flags` | integer | Bits 24 to 26: the rating |
| `query_start` | integer | The row to start from, 101 are given at most |

**Answer** (each row of `data`)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner_id` | string | Who organizes it |
| `name` | string | Its title |
| `event_id` | integer | Its identifier |
| `date` | string | When it starts, in Pacific time (`m/d h:i A`), as the viewers show it |
| `unix_time` | integer | When it starts, Unix time |
| `event_flags` | integer | The rating: 0 PG, 1 Mature, 2 Adult |
| `landing_point` | string | Where it is on the map of the world (`x,y,z`) |

| `category` | integer | The category, 0 for any |
| `query_start` | integer | The row to start from, 101 are given at most |

**Answer** (each row of `data`)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classifiedid` | string | The UUID of the classified |
| `name` | string | Its title |

### `avatar_publish_update`

The "show in search" box of a profile, which OpenSimulator ignores and the module tells here with the secure session of the avatar.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `avatar_id` | string | The UUID of the avatar |
| `secure_session_id` | string | Its secure session, which only the simulator it is connected to holds |
| `allow_publish` | string | `true` to show the profile in search |

**Answer**: `success`, with the reason in `errorMessage` when it failed.

parameters.name: gk
parameters.description: The gatekeeper of the grid the search is made for (`grid.example.org:8002`), when the search is shared: only its places are answered

400.description: The body is not an XML-RPC request

403.description: The caller does not hold the secure session of the avatar (avatar_publish_update)

404.description: The grid is not known here

503.description: The grid has no database for it, or no key for its currency

post.description:
Quotes, purchases, balances and transfers. XML-RPC at `currency.php` of the economy address of the grid. The viewer asks the quote and buys; the simulators ask the balance of the avatars who are on them, move the money of a purchase, and claim the avatars that arrive. The answer is a struct with `success`, and the reason (`errorMessage`, `errorURI`) when it is false.

### `getCurrencyQuote`

The viewer asks what an amount of currency costs.

**Request** (the struct)

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agentId` | string | The avatar |
| `secureSessionId` | string | Its secure session |
| `currencyBuy` | integer | The amount |

**Answer**

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `success` | boolean | Whether the avatar proved who they are |

A message for an avatar who is not there is kept. What the module V1 of the simulators posts to `<OfflineMessageURL>/SaveMessage/` (the last slash is theirs, it is accepted with or without).

**Request**: The `GridInstantMessage` of OpenSimulator, in XML (`fromAgentID`, `fromAgentName`, `toAgentID`, `dialog`, `message`, ...).

**Answer**: `<boolean>true</boolean>` when it was kept, `<error>` when it was not.

The messages kept for an avatar who comes back are given, and forgotten. What the module V1 of the simulators posts to `<OfflineMessageURL>/RetrieveMessages/` (the last slash is theirs, it is accepted with or without).

**Request**: The UUID of the avatar: `<UUID><Guid>...</Guid></UUID>`.

**Answer**: An `ArrayOfGridInstantMessage` with the messages, in the XML they were kept in.

post.description: The setup that a few answers stand for. A grid has its Robust and a first simulator, `Welcome`, with its region; a standalone is one simulator that is the whole grid, with the name that was given. Everything the answers do not say is what the planners propose (ports, database, folders, options), so an empty request gives the proposals. `setup` is in the format of the setup files (`opensim import`), the password of the avatar is kept hashed in it. `problems` names the questions that are wrong or missing, `rows` lists every value the setup defines.
